display.purpose: Hero headline and close footer — the one moment that stops the scroll.

title.purpose: Card titles, layer names, product names.

body.purpose: Paragraph copy, descriptions, form labels. Max ~65ch via container constraints.

label.purpose: Badges, price labels, button text, nav links, channel meta. Chip-shaped, all-caps.

shadows.name: ambient
shadows.purpose: Default card rest state — soft, warm, barely there.

shadows.name: chip
shadows.purpose: Price chips and tighter elements — more defined lift.

shadows.name: card
shadows.purpose: Hover/elevated/selected state — the hand brings the lift.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Default easing for state transitions (hover, focus, selection).

motion.name: ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: Entrance animations (layer-rise, card-rise) — fast start, gentle settle.

motion.name: stagger-step
motion.purpose: Delay between staggered entrance items (cards, layers, channels).

breakpoints.name: desktop
breakpoints.purpose: Grid activation for hero (2-col), layer list (2-col), about (3-col), product cards (3-col).

narrative.overview: A warm, schoolyard-fresh identity that feels like pressing a cold cup into your hands on a 40°C day. The system leads with appetite: mango-orange as the committed accent on a cream ground, cocoa-brown ink for warmth, and visible layers that prove the product's difference at a glance. Density is generous but never loose — sections breathe on mobile, cards cast soft ink shadows, and every interactive surface responds with a confident lift. The aesthetic rejects sterile minimalism; it chooses the friendly, slightly rounded vernacular of a student-run stall, where Comic-style display type and chip-shaped buttons feel native, not nostalgic.
keyCharacteristics: Cream ground (#fff8ec) with mango-orange (#f59e0b) as the single committed accent
Cocoa-brown ink (#3a2317) for warmth, never pure black
Baloo 2 display + Nunito body — friendly, legible, school-appropriate
Generous 18px card radius, full-pill chip radius — soft, approachable corners
Soft ink shadows that lift on interaction, not hover-only decoration
Visible layering as visual proof — the cup diagram and layer swatches are the hero
Prices (₱30/₱35) treated as first-class content, never buried

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Mango orange (#f59e0b) appears on ≤10% of any screen. Its job is to say "act now" — CTA, selected price, the hot price chip. It never decorates.

rules.name: The Edible Palette Rule
rules.body: Every non-neutral color maps to a real ingredient layer. If a color cannot be pointed to in the cup diagram, it does not belong in the system.

rules.name: The Ink Warmth Rule
rules.body: No pure black (#000). Cocoa ink (#3a2317) carries all structure; its soft variant (#6b4a33) carries all secondary text. This warmth is non-negotiable.

rules.name: The Display Rarity Rule
rules.body: Display weight (800) appears only at Display and Headline roles. Titles use 700; body never exceeds 600. The heaviness is reserved for the moments that must stop the scroll.

rules.name: The Label Shape Rule
rules.body: All-caps label text (0.08em tracking) only appears inside chip-radius containers (badges, buttons, nav pills). It never runs loose in body copy.

rules.name: The Lift-On-Intent Rule
rules.body: Shadows deepen only on hover, focus, or selection — never as static decoration. A card at rest is flat with ambient; the hand (or thumb) brings the lift.

rules.name: The Ink Shadow Rule
rules.body: All shadows use rgba(58, 35, 23, α) — cocoa ink, never neutral gray. The warmth persists in elevation.

rules.name: The Two-Radius Rule
rules.body: The system has exactly two structural radii: card (18px) and chip (999px). Layer swatches (12px) and cup silhouettes (18/28px) are component-specific exceptions, not scale steps. No radius ladder (sm/md/lg/xl).

rules.name: The Two-Pixel Border Rule
rules.body: Structural borders are 2px cocoa ink. No 1px, no variable weight. The border is a deliberate stroke, not a whisper.

dos: Do use mango orange (#f59e0b) only for primary actions, selected states, and the hot price chip. Its scarcity is its power.
Do keep all borders at 2px cocoa ink (#3a2317). The stroke weight is part of the warm, hand-made feel.
Do pair Baloo 2 800 with Nunito 400/600/700. The display family owns headlines, badges, and buttons; body owns prose.
Do lift cards on hover/focus/selection (translateY -2px to -4px + card shadow). Depth responds to intent.
Do show prices (₱30/₱35) in display-weight Baloo 2 at every decision point — hero, layer list, product cards, form total.
Do make the layer diagram interactive. The cup is not illustration; it's the spec.
Do use the landscape gradients (--bg-landscape-1/2/3) per section. They shift warmth without changing the ground.
donts: Don't introduce a second accent color. Mango orange is the one committed color; flan gold, mango fruit, graham, etc. are layer-semantic, not UI accents.
Don't use pure black (#000) or cool grays. Cocoa ink (#3a2317) and its soft variant carry all structure.
Don't add radius steps (sm/md/lg). The system has card (18px) and chip (999px). Component-specific radii (cup 18/28, swatch 12) are exceptions, not scale.
Don't use hairline (1px) borders. The 2px ink stroke is deliberate.
Don't make the mock checkout look real. The "Demo only" toast, hidden action, and labeled demo contract are non-negotiable honesty.
Don't hide the layers. The visible layering is the differentiation; every section should reinforce it.
Don't use box-shadow for static decoration. Shadows only deepen on interaction (hover, focus, selection).
